03

How a project runs

Brief → live
01

Blockout and budget

Before anything is modelled properly, I build the scene in grey boxes at real-world scale and agree the budget — triangle count, texture memory, target frame rate, target device. Everything after this is measured against those numbers.

3ds MaxUnreal
02

Asset production

High-poly sculpt, retopology, UVs at a consistent texel density, then bakes and PBR texturing. Props go into a kit so the same pieces rebuild later scenes instead of being modelled twice.

3ds MaxSubstanceZBrush
03

Engine assembly and lighting

Assets land in Unreal or Unity with LODs and collision already set. Lighting is built for the actual viewing condition — a bright showroom tablet needs different exposure from a dark VR headset.

Unreal 5Unity URPLumen
04

Optimisation pass

Profile, then fix what the profiler actually shows: draw calls merged, shaders simplified, textures right-sized, occlusion set up. I'd rather cut a feature than ship something that stutters.

Unreal InsightsRenderDocProfiler
05

Web layer and handover

The part most 3D projects skip. Auth, data, admin screens, a CI build and a real deploy — so the client can log in, change content and ship updates without calling me every week.

Next.jsNodeDocker
04

About

Maryam M. Shoaib Manama, BH

I sit between two teams that usually don't talk to each other. Artists hand over beautiful scenes that no browser can load; web developers build solid apps with a grey box where the product should be. I've spent my career on both sides of that gap, which means I can take a project from a modelling brief all the way to a URL a client can send to their customers.

Most of my work starts in 3ds Max and ends in Unreal Engine or Unity — architectural walkthroughs, product visualisation, VR training, game-ready asset kits. When a project needs to live on the web instead of in an executable, I rebuild it in Three.js and WebGL and keep the same look at a fraction of the download.

I work from Bahrain with clients across the Gulf and remotely further afield, in English, Arabic and Urdu. I care about frame budgets, honest timelines, and shipping things that still work six months after handover.
